attributes.body_ja:
「さえ〜ば」は、副助詞（ふくじょし）の「さえ」と接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）の「ば」からできた仮定的（かていてき）な表現（ひょうげん）です。(A) を条件（じょうけん）として示（しめ）して、「もし (A) であれば、(B) が実現（じつげん）できる」や「(B) を実現（じつげん）するために必要（ひつよう）なのは (A) だけだ」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「さえ」は、どのような品詞（ひんし）にも使（つか）えますが、動詞（どうし）は連用形（れんようけい）かテ形（てけい）にする必要（ひつよう）があります。また、「さえ」の前（まえ）に助詞（じょし）が付（つ）くこともあります。

この用法（ようほう）の「さえ」は、(A) 「だけ」が条件（じょうけん）であることを表（あらわ）します。そして、「ば」がその条件（じょうけん）が満（み）たされることを仮定（かてい）します。「さえ」は「ば」以外（いがい）の助詞（じょし）（「たら」など）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われることもありますが、「さえ〜ば」は決（き）まった表現（ひょうげん）として扱（あつか）われているので、「ば」が使（つか）われることがほとんどです。
attributes.body:
As a set expression, さえ～ば is a combination of the adverbial particle さえ, and the conjunction particle ば. It is used to highlight assumption, and presents (A) as a extreme limitation that is required to achieve (B), hypothetically. This structure may be translated as 'if only (A), then (B)', 'the only thing needed for (B) is (A)', or 'as long as (A), (B)'.

さえ may be grouped with any word, but will require the conjunctive form, or て form before it when grouped with verbs. It also regularly appears after other particles, forming a dual-particle meaning.

This use of さえ is an example of limit, with (A) being a hypothetical limit presented by the ば particle. It is also possible to see さえ with other hypothetical indicators (such as たら), but is quite rare in modern Japanese, as さえ～ば is considered a set pattern.

This limitation is also sometimes referred to as a 'stipulation', or 'condition'.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both expressions use さえ, but their usages and nuances differ. さえ〜ば shows that one condition is sufficient, like 'as long as (A)', e.g. お金さえあれば何とかなる ('As long as I have money, things will work out'). さえ alone emphasizes extremity, surprise, or unexpectedness, e.g. 彼さえ知らない ('Even he doesn't know').

first_relatable.title: さえ〜ば
first_relatable.meaning: If only…then, As long as..., Provided..., Only thing ... needs for ... is ...

attributes.body: These expressions both connect a condition to a result, but in different ways. さえ〜ば emphasizes that the condition alone is enough, e.g. お金さえあれば大丈夫 ('As long as I have money, I'll be fine'). からには highlights an obligation or natural consequence once a condition is true, e.g. 仕事を引き受けたからには最後までやる ('Since I took on the task, I'll see it through').

first_relatable.title: さえ〜ば
first_relatable.meaning: If only…then, As long as..., Provided..., Only thing ... needs for ... is ...

attributes.body: Both expressions can be translated as 'as long as (A)', but they differ in nuance. さえ〜ば indicates that a single condition is sufficient, e.g. 努力さえすればうまくいく ('As long as you try, things will go well'). 限り means 'as long as' in the sense of duration or ongoing state, e.g. 生きている限り夢を追いたい ('As long as I live, I want to chase my dream').
